subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what safety semantics should it use for failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config and user-visible failed-mutation behavior; source inspection proves the gap, but maintainers must choose whether operators may hide warnings that currently protect users from silent false success.

options.title: Add default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default plus explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep the boolean only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and narrow this issue to docs or specific remaining channel leaks.

options.title: Split narrow leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and handle channel-specific or tool-class-specific leaks in separate issues before designing a shared policy.

recommendation.title: Add default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default plus explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged warning-policy fix that left this issue as the broader config/policy follow-up.
